question: In tennis, the court should be _________ wide for a doubles match as per the International Tennis Federation.
solution:
The correct answer is __**36ft**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the International Tennis Federation (ITF), the standard width of a tennis court for doubles matches is **36 feet (10.97 meters)**.
 
• The doubles court is wider than the singles court, which measures **27 feet (8.23 meters) in width**, to accommodate the additional players on each team.
 
• The total length of a doubles tennis court remains the same as a singles court: **78 feet (23.77 meters)**.
 
• The extra width in doubles courts is provided by the “doubles alleys,” which are the areas between the singles sidelines and the doubles sidelines.
 
• The court dimensions for doubles are consistent across all levels of play, from amateur to professional, as regulated by the ITF.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **International Tennis Federation (ITF):**

 
 
• The ITF is the governing body of world tennis and is responsible for defining and maintaining the rules of the game.
 
• It ensures consistent court dimensions and standards across international tournaments.
 
 
 
• **Doubles Alley:**
 
 
• The area on a tennis court between the singles and doubles sidelines, used only in doubles matches.
 
• The width of the doubles alley on each side is 4.5 feet (1.37 meters), making the total extra width 9 feet (2.74 meters).
 
 
 
• **Standard Court Surface Types:**
 
 
• The main types of tennis court surfaces are clay, grass, and hard courts, each affecting the speed and bounce of the ball.
 
• The dimensions of the court remain the same regardless of the surface type.
 
 
 
• **Key Court Markings:**
 
 
• **Baseline:** The back boundary line of the court, running parallel to the net.
 
• **Sidelines:** The outer boundaries of the court that vary for singles and doubles matches.
 
• **Service Boxes:** The rectangular areas on each side of the net where the serve must land.
 
 
 
• **Net Height:**
 
 
• The net height at the center is **3 feet (0.914 meters)**, and at the posts, it is **3.5 feet (1.07 meters).**
 
• The net divides the court into two equal halves for play.
